v.why: An identity edge 0->3 turns the 0->1->3 conv path into a residual refinement that trains easily, so adding a 3x3 on edge 4 yields more when edge 3 is a skip.
When edge 3 is absent, a skip on edge 5 opens a short gradient-friendly route to the output that substitutes for the missing bypass.
A parallel 3x3 from the input already supplies conv features at summing node 2, so a second 3x3 on edge 2 has diminishing returns.
A 3x3 on edge 4 already feeds conv features to the output, so converting edge 3 into another 3x3 gains less and also forfeits a possible shortcut.
When node 1 holds 3x3 features, a skip on edge 4 forwards a learned conv branch to the output, whereas after a non-conv edge 0 it forwards near-raw input.
With edge 4 as identity, node 1 is forwarded directly to the output, so a conv on edge 0 becomes a guaranteed conv branch to node 3 and its value rises.
Without a direct input-to-output edge every output signal passes through node 1 or 2, so the transformation on edge 0 dominates accuracy and a 3x3 there matters more.
With edge 5 as identity, a 3x3 on edge 1 forms a direct conv branch from input to output, whereas a none or weak edge 5 limits how much edge-1 features reach node 3.
An identity bypass around a conv-terminated deep path turns the cell into a residual block, so making edge 3 a skip helps more when edge 5 is a 3x3.
Without a direct input-to-output edge the input reaches node 3 only via nodes 1 and 2, so a 3x3 on edge 1 becomes a primary feature source and its value increases.
